chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is-haq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about voluntary prayers near the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the shrines of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and the two Holy Sanctuaries, and performing voluntary prayers in them while we are deficient (in obligatory prayers). He said: 'Yes, perform voluntary prayers as much as you are able; it is good.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Holy Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina)
key_terms.مُقَصِّرُونَ: Those who are deficient/lacking (in obligatory duties)

ai.seo_question: Can I perform voluntary prayers at a shrine if I haven't prayed my obligatory prayers yet?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Rida (AS) affirming that performing voluntary prayers at the shrines of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Holy Masjids is meritorious even for those who are 'muqassirun' (those who have missed or are short on obligatory prayers). This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of the shrines as places of grace, encouraging believers not to be deterred by their ritual shortcomings from seeking proximity to the Imams. It underscores the principle that voluntary acts of devotion at these sacred sites carry independent weight and reward.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from ‘Ali ibn Ismā’īl, from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār, who said:

I asked Abal Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) if a Muqassir can establish voluntary prayers next to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.), at (different holy) sites of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.), and in the two Ḥarams. Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes. Establish as many voluntary prayers as you can for it is a blessing.”
